oneLine: Interest you earn on your savings and on earlier interest.
explanation: Compound interest is interest on interest. The bank pays interest on your money. Next time, it also pays interest on that interest.
Over many years, this makes savings grow faster. The longer the money stays, the bigger the effect.
whyItMatters: Starting early gives compound interest more time to work. Small amounts saved when you are young can grow large. The same effect makes unpaid debt grow fast.
workedExample: You save $1,000 at 5% a year. After one year, you have $1,050. In the second year, you earn 5% on $1,050, which is $52.50. After 10 years, you have about $1,629.
